results.title: Abstract statement
results.statement_summary: A ⊂ R^n Borel, W_0: A → G(n,m) Lipschitzian; limsup_{r→0+} H^m[A ∩ B(x,r) ∩ (x+W_0(x))]/(α(m) r^m) ≥ 1/2^n for L^n-a.e. x ∈ A; plus a negligibility equivalence whose parenthesis is literally unbalanced in the source.
results.reason: Restates the conclusion of Theorem 8.4 (existing record 2111); the accompanying equivalence sentence compresses Theorem 8.1, with the literal defect recorded in SCOPE_BOUNDARIES.

results.title: French abstract statement
results.statement_summary: Same as the abstract, in French.
results.reason: Translation of the abstract; no separate mathematical content; the same literal defect occurs at line 171.

results.title: Zygmund conjecture as an attributed (reportedly) conjecture
results.statement_summary: Assume x ↦ L(x) is a Lipschitzian field of lines with x ∈ L(x) and f: R^2 → R square summable; is f(x) = lim_{r→0+} average over L(x) ∩ B(x,r) of f w.r.t. H^1, for L^2-a.e. x ∈ R^2?
results.reason: Explicitly presented as a conjecture reportedly attributed to Zygmund; the paper does NOT prove it. Registered as an open question, never as an author-proved conclusion.

results.title: Foreword italic lower-density statement (n = 2, lines)
results.statement_summary: Lipschitz field of lines with x ∈ L(x), A ⊂ R^2 Lebesgue measurable: limsup_{r→0+} H^1(A ∩ B(x,r) ∩ L(x))/(2r) ≥ 1/4 for L^2-a.e. x ∈ A.
results.reason: Special case n = 2, m = 1, α(1) = 2 of Theorem 8.4; a dimensional specialization, hence no separate core. Its lead-in at 212 explicitly restricts the paper's claim to indicator functions.

results.title: Foreword nonparallel Fubini-type corollary
results.statement_summary: A is Lebesgue negligible iff H^1(A ∩ L(x)) = 0 for L^2-a.e. x ∈ R^2.
results.reason: Informal n = 2 form of Theorem 8.1; here the a.e. variable is x ∈ R^2, whereas Theorem 8.1 quantifies x ∈ A in (3.2) and x ∈ S in (3.3). The differing quantifier sites are recorded literally in SCOPE_BOUNDARIES and not harmonized.

results.title: Unnumbered Foreword theorem: three equivalent conditions
results.statement_summary: W_0: R^n → G(n,m) Lipschitzian, A ⊂ R^n Borel; (A) L^n(A)=0; (B) for L^n-a.e. x ∈ A, H^m(A ∩ (x+W_0(x)))=0; (C) for L^n-a.e. x ∈ R^n, H^m(A ∩ (x+W_0(x)))=0; equivalent.
results.reason: Unnumbered Foreword restatement of Theorem 8.1 (there with W_0 on S and A ⊂ S); same mathematical content, so no separate candidate.

results.title: Unnumbered Sketch theorem: the main density bound
results.statement_summary: W(x) = x + W_0(x); limsup_{r→0+} H^m(A ∩ B(x,r) ∩ W(x))/(α(m)r^m) ≥ 1/2^n for L^n-a.e. x ∈ A.
results.reason: Unnumbered restatement inside the Sketch of Theorem 8.4 (existing 2111); identical statement and constant.

results.title: Standing conventions: 1 ≤ m ≤ n−1, ambient R^n, inner product, Borel σ-algebra
results.statement_summary: 1 ≤ m ≤ n−1 integers; ambient space R^n; ⟨x,x'⟩ and Euclidean |x|; B(S) the Borel σ-algebra of S.
results.reason: Notation only; fixes the range 1 ≤ m ≤ n−1 used by every later result.

results.title: Hausdorff measure, its normalization, and three elementary facts
results.statement_summary: L^n Lebesgue outer measure, α(n)=L^n(B(0,1)), ζ^m(S)=α(m)2^{-m}(diam S)^m, δ-covers, H^m_δ and H^m. (2.1) H^m_∞ is upper semicontinuous along Hausdorff-convergent compacta; (2.2) on R^m, L^m = H^m = H^m_∞; (2.3) on an m-dimensional affine subspace, H^m = H^m_∞.
results.reason: Textbook measure theory with full elementary proofs; fixes the normalization behind the constant, but no new core.

results.title: Coarea formula (Euclidean and rectifiable versions) and exterior-power bounds
results.statement_summary: Federer coarea for Lipschitz f: A → R^{n−m}, Jf = sqrt|det(Df∘Df*)| = ||∧_{n−m}Df||; rectifiable version with J_A f; (eq.11) norm of ∧_k L as a supremum; (eq.12) lower bound by the volume ratio of k independent vectors; both hold for locally Lipschitz f by monotone convergence.
results.reason: Cited standard machinery (Evans–Gariepy, GMT); an input to the old core, not new material.

results.title: Grassmannian as a compact metric space; Lipschitz retraction and Lipschitz extension of fields
results.statement_summary: G(n,m) with d(W_1,W_2)=||P_{W_1}−P_{W_2}||; W ↦ W^⊥ is an isometry onto G(n,n−m); identification with M_{n,m}; existence of a Lipschitz retraction ρ and hence of a Lipschitz extension of any Lipschitz W_0: S → G(n,m) to a neighborhood.
results.reason: Standard metric and retraction facts (GMT 3.1.20, 2.10.43); supports localization only.

results.title: Stiefel manifold of orthonormal m-frames
results.statement_summary: V(n,m) = {(w_1,...,w_m): orthonormal} with the metric inherited from (R^n)^m.
results.reason: Notation only.

results.title: Lipschitz frame parameterization on a small-diameter closed set of planes
results.statement_summary: For nonempty closed V ⊂ G(n,m) with diam V < 1 there is Lipschitz Ξ: V → V(n,m) with W = span{Ξ_1(W),...,Ξ_m(W)}.
results.reason: Projection plus Gram–Schmidt with explicit Lipschitz estimates (proof 524-536); routine, used to build local frames.

results.title: Borel measurable frame selection on the whole Grassmannian
results.statement_summary: There is Borel Ξ: G(n,m) → V(n,m) spanning each W.
results.reason: Piecewise application of 3.6 on finitely many Borel pieces of diameter ≤ 1/2 (proof 545-548); routine selection.

results.title: Local Lipschitz orthonormal frames adapted to a Lipschitz plane field
results.statement_summary: For S ⊂ R^n, x_0 ∈ S, W_0: S → G(n,m) Lipschitzian: there are a neighborhood U and Lipschitz w_1..w_m, v_1..v_{n−m}: U → R^n forming an orthonormal basis, spanning W_0(x) and W_0(x)^⊥ for x ∈ S ∩ U.
results.reason: Combination of 3.4 and 3.6 (proof 566-573); technical localization used throughout, including in the 8.1 proof.

results.title: Global Borel orthonormal frames adapted to a Borel plane field
results.statement_summary: For Borel W_0: R^n → G(n,m) there are Borel w_1..w_m, v_1..v_{n−m} forming an orthonormal basis with the required spans at every point.
results.reason: Immediate from 3.7 (proof 590-597); measurability bookkeeping.

results.title: Convention W(x) = x + W_0(x)
results.statement_summary: Affine subspace through x with direction W_0(x) whenever W_0(x) is defined; U may be repeatedly shrunk.
results.reason: Convention fixing the object measured by H^m in every statement.

results.title: Definition of g_{v_1..v_{n−m},u} and derivation of a coarea-factor lower bound
results.reason: Definition of the auxiliary map plus the elementary perturbation computation formalized as 3.12; the same computation is used inside the old core, so it is recorded as definition plus derivation, not as a separate core.

results.title: Quantitative lower bound J g ≥ 1−ε at small diameter
results.statement_summary: For Λ>0, 0<ε<1 there is δ(n,Λ,ε)>0 such that if U is open, u ∈ R^n, v_i: U → R^n Lipschitz with Lip ≤ Λ and pointwise orthonormal, and diam(U ∪ {u}) ≤ δ, then Jg_{v_1..v_{n−m},u}(x) ≥ 1−ε for L^n-a.e. x ∈ U.
results.reason: Elementary determinant perturbation bound (derived in prose 607-665); standard quantitative stability of the Jacobian, used as an input in 7.5.

results.title: Definition of π_u and identification of its level sets with W(x)
results.statement_summary: π_u(ξ_1..ξ_{n−m},x)=(⟨ξ_i,x−u⟩)_i; π_{ξ,u}^{-1}{y} is an m-dimensional affine subspace; in the adapted-frame setting π_{v_1(x)..v_{n−m}(x),u}^{-1}{g(x)}=W(x).
results.reason: Notation and a direct verification; identity (eq.4) feeds the measurability arguments.

results.title: Borel measurability of (ξ,y) ↦ H^m(B ∩ π_{ξ,u}^{-1}{y})
results.statement_summary: For B Borel and u fixed, that map on V(n,n−m) × R^{n−m} is Borel.
results.reason: Upper semicontinuity for compact B via Hausdorff convergence, then a Dynkin-class argument (proof 726-754); standard descriptive measurability.

results.title: Borel measurability of x ↦ H^m(B ∩ W(x))
results.statement_summary: For B Borel and W_0 Borel, that function is Borel.
results.reason: Factorization through 3.14 (proof 766-780); measurability bookkeeping needed to define φ.

results.title: Definition of the measure φ_{E,W}(B) = ∫_E H^m(B ∩ W(x)) dL^n(x)
results.statement_summary: For Borel W_0 and Borel E with L^n(E)<∞; locally finite Borel measure with φ_{E,W}(B) ≤ α(m)(diam B)^m L^n(E).
results.reason: Central definition of the paper, but a definition rather than a proved core.

results.title: Definition of nearly m-Nikodym set (absolute and relative versions)
results.statement_summary: B ∈ B(E) is nearly m-Nikodym in E if L^n(B)>0 and for L^n-a.e. x ∈ E there is W ∈ G(n,m) with H^m(B ∩ (x+W))=0; relative version with a prescribed Borel field: H^m(B ∩ W(x))=0 for a.e. x ∈ E. Cites Nikodym (n=2, m=1) and Falconer (m=n−1).
results.reason: Definition plus literature pointers for the motivating examples; no author proof is claimed for those examples.

results.title: Equivalence: L^n absolutely continuous w.r.t. φ_{E,W} ⇔ no nearly m-Nikodym set
results.statement_summary: For E Borel of finite measure and W_0 Borel: L^n restricted to B(E) is absolutely continuous w.r.t. φ_{E,W} restricted to B(E) iff there is no nearly m-Nikodym set in E relative to W.
results.reason: Two-line proof (828-831); immediate unpacking of the definitions.

results.title: Every nearly m-Nikodym set is relative to some Borel field, and to some continuous field on a compact piece
results.statement_summary: (19.1) there is Borel W_0: R^n → G(n,m) with B nearly m-Nikodym in E relative to W; (19.2) there are compact C ⊂ B and continuous W̄_0 with C nearly m-Nikodym in C relative to W̄.
results.reason: Independent selection statement assessed on its own: Borel incidence encoding845-866, named vonNeumann selection867-872, Lusin/continuous extension/retraction874-879. After these standard inputs the remaining composition has no independent advanced construction or estimate. Its absence from8.1/8.4is not the exclusion reason.
results.producer_reason: von Neumann selection + Lusin + retraction (proof 845-880), a standard descriptive-set-theoretic selection. It is not used in the proofs of 8.1 or 8.4 (it only supports the remark at 263 on why Lipschitz regularity is the relevant hypothesis), so it carries no load toward any candidate.

results.title: Setting for Sections 5-7
results.statement_summary: E ⊂ R^n Borel with L^n(E)<∞; U open with E ⊂ U; B ⊂ R^n Borel; W_0: U → G(n,m) Lipschitzian; W(x)=x+W_0(x); Λ>0; w_i, v_i: U → R^n with Lip ≤ Λ, spanning W_0(x) and W_0(x)^⊥ pointwise and forming an orthonormal basis.
results.reason: Hypothesis package shared by the quantitative part; it is the localization supplied by 3.8.

results.title: First fibration Σ = F(E × R^m) ⊂ R^n × R^n and the coarea identities
results.statement_summary: F(x,t)=(x, x+Σt_iw_i(x)); Σ={(x,u): x ∈ E, u ∈ W(x)} is countably (n+m)-rectifiable; Σ_B=Σ ∩ π_2^{-1}(B); slice identities (eq.6), (eq.8); coarea identities (eq.9) and (eq.10); the tangent space is generated by the listed n+m vectors.
results.reason: Exactly the 'two rectifiable fibrations' construction already counted inside the H3 core of 2111; reused, not recounted.

results.title: Two-sided bound for the coarea Jacobian of π_1 on Σ
results.reason: Explicit quantitative coarea Jacobian bound named in the existing H3 reason ('quantitative coarea Jacobian bounds'); proof 980-1020 reused.

results.title: Existence of a coordinate projection making an orthonormal family a well-conditioned matrix
results.statement_summary: For orthonormal v_1..v_q in R^n there is λ ∈ Λ(n,q) with |det(⟨v_k,e_{λ(j)}⟩)| ≥ binom(n,q)^{-1/2}.
results.reason: Binet–Cauchy pigeonhole (proof 1033-1042); a linear-algebra lemma supporting 5.4.

results.title: Bounds and strict positivity for the coarea Jacobian of π_2 on Σ
results.statement_summary: (24.1) explicit lower bound (binom(n,n−m)^{-1/2} − m(n−m)Λ|x−u|(1+mΛ|x−u|)^{n−m−1})/(2+2mΛ|x−u|+m^2Λ^2|x−u|^2)^{(n−m)/2} ≤ J_Σπ_2 ≤ 1; (24.2) J_Σπ_2 > 0 H^{n+m}-a.e. on Σ, via a rank set, a polynomial that does not vanish at 0, and Fubini.
results.reason: Quantitative Jacobian bound plus the positivity that drives absolute continuity; part of the old H3 core's coarea apparatus (proof 1061-1139).

results.title: φ_{E,W} is absolutely continuous with respect to L^n
results.statement_summary: The measure φ_{E,W} of 3.16 is absolutely continuous w.r.t. L^n.
results.reason: Five-line consequence of (eq.10) and 5.4(24.2) (proof 1146-1157); no new mechanism. It is imported by the 8.1 proof.

results.title: Definition of the Radon–Nikodym density Z_E W
results.statement_summary: φ_{E,W}(B)=∫_B (Z_E W) dL^n; Borel representative, unique up to L^n-null sets, fixed once and for all.
results.reason: Definition resting on 5.5.

results.title: Definition of Y^0_E W(u) = H^m(E ∩ g_u^{-1}{0})
results.statement_summary: L^n-measurable function of u; comparable to Z_E W at small diameter by 5.8.
results.reason: Definition; also explains (line 1231) why a further covariable is required.

results.title: Two-sided comparability of Z_E W and Y^0_E W at small diameter
results.statement_summary: (1−ε)2^{-(n−m)/2} Y^0_E W(u) ≤ Z_E W(u) ≤ (1+ε)2^{(n−m)/2} binom(n,n−m)^{1/2} Y^0_E W(u) for L^n-a.e. u ∈ E, provided diam E ≤ δ(n,Λ,ε).
results.reason: Direct comparison obtained by sandwiching the coarea identities with the Jacobian bounds (proof 1196-1226); constant bookkeeping inside the old core.

results.title: Rest stop: why a second covariable is added
results.statement_summary: The upper bound for Z_E W follows from 6.4; to get Z_E W > 0 one adds y ∈ R^{n−m}, because u is not the covariable of a function whose level sets are measured in (eq.14).
results.reason: Pure motivation; no mathematical claim.

results.title: Second fibration with the covariable y: Σ̂_r and the coarea identities
results.statement_summary: F̂_r(x,t,y)=(x, x+Σt_iw_i(x)+Σy_iv_i(x), y) on E × R^m × C_r; Σ̂_r countably 2n-rectifiable; slice identities for π_1×π_3 and π_2×π_3 give the appropriate H^m's; coarea identities (eq.20), (eq.21).
results.reason: The second rectifiable fibration named in the existing H3 reason; reused, not recounted.

results.title: Jacobian bounds on the second fibration
results.reason: Quantitative 2n-dimensional Jacobian bound (proof 1323-1389), again part of the old H3 coarea support; it is also the source of the factor 2^{-(n−m)}.

results.title: Definition of Y_E W(u) = liminf_j average over C_{j^{-1}} of H^m(E ∩ g_u^{-1}{y})
results.statement_summary: L^n-measurable; Y_F W ≤ Y_E W for F ⊂ E; replaces Y^0_E W.
results.reason: Auxiliaryfunctionaldefinedbyliminf_javeragesatreciprocalradii j^{-1};native1405/1426andoriginalphysical25. It is not a dyadic sequence.
results.producer_reason: Definition of the central lower-bound functional (liminf of dyadic averages of level measures).

results.title: Measurability and uniform bound for the auxiliary averages f_j
results.statement_summary: x ↦ average over C_{j^{-1}} of H^m(B ∩ (W(x)+Σy_iv_i(x))) dL^{n−m}(y) is L^n-measurable; if B is bounded then |f_j(x)| ≤ α(m)(diam B)^m.
results.reason: Fubini-level measurability and the domination needed for the reverse Fatou step in 5.15.

results.title: Upper semicontinuity in y of H^m(B ∩ (W(x)+Σy_iv_i(x))) for compact B
results.statement_summary: For compact B and each x ∈ E, y ↦ H^m(B ∩ (W(x)+Σy_iv_i(x))) is upper semicontinuous.
results.reason: Same Hausdorff-convergence argument as 3.14 (proof 1443-1455); standard.

results.title: Lower bound of the integral of H^m(B ∩ W(x)) over E by (1−ε)2^{-(n−m)} times the integral of Y_E W over B
results.statement_summary: For 0<ε<1 there is δ(n,Λ,ε)>0 such that if diam(E ∪ B) ≤ δ and B is compact, then the stated inequality holds.
results.reason: The quantitative near-full-volume lower-bound mechanism (proof 1466-1509: coarea on Σ̂, upper semicontinuity, reverse Fatou, Fatou) that the existing H3 reason attributes to the old core; reused, not recounted.

results.title: Pointwise lower bound Z_E W ≥ (1−ε)2^{-(n−m)} Y_E W at small diameter
results.statement_summary: If 0<ε<1 and diam E ≤ δ_{lb.1}(n,Λ,ε), then Z_E W(u) ≥ (1−ε)2^{-(n−m)}Y_E W(u) for L^n-a.e. u ∈ E.
results.reason: Immediate consequence of 5.15 through the Radon–Nikodym definition; the source gives the statement with no proof environment.

results.title: Bow tie lemma: a set nearly contained in a plane is a Lipschitz graph over it
results.statement_summary: If for all x ∈ S and 0<ρ≤diam S, S ∩ B(x,ρ) ⊂ B(x+W,τρ) with 0<τ<1, then S = im F with F: P_W(S) → R^n, Lip F ≤ 1/sqrt(1−τ^2); hence H^m(S) ≤ (1/sqrt(1−τ^2))^m α(m)(diam S)^m.
results.reason: Elementary geometry (proof 1536-1549); supplies the upper-bound constant in 6.3, standard folklore.

results.title: Level sets of g_u are nearly contained in the plane W_0(x_0)
results.statement_summary: For 0<τ<1 there is δ(n,Λ,τ)>0 such that if diam(E ∪ {x_0} ∪ {u}) ≤ δ, then for every y, every x ∈ E ∩ g_u^{-1}{y} and every ρ>0: E ∩ g_u^{-1}{y} ∩ B(x,ρ) ⊂ B(x+W_0(x_0),τρ).
results.reason: The explicit constant δ = τ/(2Λ√n) and the two-step Lipschitz estimate (proof 1566-1587) are the transverse-ball ingredient that makes the nonlinear leaves nearly planar; already counted in the old H3 reason.

results.title: Upper bound max{Y^0_E W(u), Y_E W(u)} ≤ c(m)(diam E)^m
results.statement_summary: There are δ(n,Λ)>0 and c(m) ≥ 1 such that if diam(E ∪ {u}) ≤ δ then max{Y^0_E W(u),Y_E W(u)} ≤ c(m)(diam E)^m.
results.reason: Combination of 6.2 with 6.1 at τ = 1/2 (proof 1597-1608); no new mechanism, gives the constant (2/√3)^m α(m).

results.title: Upper bound Z_E W(u) ≤ c(n)(diam E)^m
results.statement_summary: There are δ(n,Λ)>0 and c(n) ≥ 1 such that if diam E ≤ δ then Z_E W(u) ≤ c(n)(diam E)^m for L^n-a.e. u ∈ E.
results.reason: The proof (1619-1621) only fixes δ = min{δ_{upper.bound}, δ_{Z.1}(n,Λ,1/2)}: an author-compressed verification combining 6.3 with 5.8; no new core.

results.title: Setting for Section 7 (same hypotheses as 4.1)
results.statement_summary: Re-enforces the assumptions of 4.1; C_r = {|y| ≤ r} in R^{n−m}.
results.reason: Restatement of hypotheses.

results.title: Polyballs C_W(x_0,r) defined by the two orthogonal projections
results.statement_summary: If x ∈ C_W(x_0,r) then |x−x_0| ≤ r√2; diam C_W(x_0,r) ≤ 2√2 r; L^n(C_W(x_0,r)) = α(m)α(n−m)r^n.
results.reason: Defines the non-Euclidean density basis used in Sections 7-8 (product of an m-ball and an (n−m)-ball).

results.title: Measure of a nonlinear stripe inside a polyball
results.statement_summary: For 0<ε<1/3 there is δ(n,Λ,ε)>0 such that if 0<r<δ, u ∈ C_W(x_0,r) ⊂ U, |g_u(x_0)| ≤ (1−3ε)r and C ⊂ C_{εr} is closed, then L^n(C_W(x_0,r) ∩ g_u^{-1}(C)) ≥ (1+ε)^{-1}α(m)r^m L^{n−m}(C).
results.reason: The nonlinear-stripe lower bound: four claims (Lip bound; differential close to identity; image contains a ball via intermediate values and, for m<n−1, a cited homology result; measure comparison) followed by Fubini (1661-1772). Named in the existing H3 reason ('select transverse balls whose nonlinear stripes remain disjoint'); reused, not recounted.

results.title: Geometric imagery for the stripes
results.statement_summary: Under 7.3 the set C_W(x_0,r) ∩ g_u^{-1}(C) is a 'nonlinear stripe', horizontal with respect to W_0(x_0), at height g_u(x_0) and of width C.
results.reason: Explicitly presented as imagery to help the reader; no assertion.

results.title: Lower bound for the integral of Y_{A∩C_W(x_0,r)} W over the polyball
results.statement_summary: For 0<ε<1/3 there is δ(n,Λ,ε)>0 such that if 0<r<δ, C_W(x_0,r) ⊂ U, A ⊂ U closed and L^n(A ∩ C_W(x_0,r)) ≥ (1−ε)L^n(C_W(x_0,r)), then the integral of Y_{A∩C_W} W over C_W(x_0,r) is ≥ (1−c(n)ε)α(m)r^m L^n(C_W(x_0,r)).
results.reason: Proof 1792-1922 builds a Vitali family of small balls in the y-variable, applies 3.12 and 7.3 to slightly shrunken stripes, and proves disjointness of the Ŝ_k ∩ C_W by a quantitative separation estimate (claim 1853-1887). This is the near-full-volume lower bound and the disjointness mechanism of the old H3 core; reused, not recounted.

results.title: Lower bound for the integral of Y_{A∩C_W(x_0,r)} W over A ∩ C_W(x_0,r)
results.statement_summary: Same hypotheses as 7.5; conclusion with integration over A ∩ C_W(x_0,r) and constant (1−c(n)ε)α(m)r^m L^n(C_W(x_0,r)).
results.reason: The source proof (1943-1952) is the terse 'The reader will happily check that ... suits their needs', with δ and c(n) given explicitly. Recorded as an author-compressed verification; not expanded or filled in here.

results.title: Difference between 7.5 and 7.6
results.statement_summary: Only the (smaller) domain of integration on the left-hand side differs.
results.reason: One-sentence clarification.

results.title: Positivity of Z_E W almost everywhere in E at small diameter
results.statement_summary: There is δ(n,Λ)>0 such that if diam E ≤ δ then Z_E W(u) > 0 for L^n-a.e. u ∈ E.
results.reason: Proof 1965-1986: reduce to Y_E W > 0 via 5.16; if Z = {Y_E W = 0} had positive measure, use that the polyballs form a density basis (bounded eccentricity), apply 7.6 to a compact A ⊂ Z to obtain a positive integral, contradicting Y_{A∩C_W} ≤ Y_E W = 0 on A ∩ C_W. Precisely the step the existing H3 reason calls the near-full-volume lower bound closing the contradiction; reused.

results.title: Equivalence: L^n(A)=0, H^m(A ∩ W(x))=0 a.e. on A, and H^m(A ∩ W(x))=0 a.e. on S
